summary: Independent Q4 reconstruction finds substantial legitimate F2P/P2P coverage, but bidirectional alignment is not clean. The verifier contains a grading-relevant reconciliation/convergence contradiction, one undocumented internal publish-attempt assertion, and several material coverage gaps: model-valid payload/origin mismatch detection, durable quarantine evidence, a real production-path same-payload preservation check, fencing revalidation after an in-flight publish crosses an epoch transition, verify-generated report correctness, and preservation of the archived controller log. The instruction itself remains a natural handoff and the delegated continuity contract is discoverable; the failure is semantic alignment/coverage rather than evidence insufficiency or spec-dump shape.

evidence.observation: Q4 must independently build a bidirectional requirement/test matrix; any material phantom test, untested material requirement, or grading-relevant ambiguity requires REVISE.
The role decision right is complete, unambiguous bidirectional alignment between solver-visible specification and verifier semantics.

Packet binds this review to task commit 0fe5c749b7b1e389ef764032ce65a38676b51e8d, control-plane commit c5c59e504d79992df45e80c21ae3b460f5bc26dc, PROCEDURAL isolation, the declared evidence set, result schema, and output path.

The handoff requires preserving captured incident history, keeping the event envelope/operator entrypoints, safe exact-once recovery, crash-safe consumers, held ambiguous generation resets, retention authority, and truthful final health/reconciliation reports; it delegates durability/replay detail to /app/continuity/docs/.

The delegated contract defines stable identity/origin metadata, source topology, positive physical-stream publish acknowledgement, effect/checkpoint ordering, quarantine evidence, identity-based reconciliation, highest contiguous archive-origin sequence, required-consumer progress, same-watermark convergence, replay selection, fencing, retention pins/horizon, diagnostic non-mutation, verify report paths, and preservation of incident evidence.

Primary verifier module contains F2P coverage for identity, publication, generation, topology, consumer effects, reconciliation, replay, retention and fencing plus P2P preservation for distinct events, monotonic generations, successful checkpointing, cleanup and lease renewal.

Secondary verifier module independently checks materialized reports against SQLite state, samples captured ops evidence, checks diagnostic non-mutation, stale release, minimum-age/hold behavior, historical generation preservation, and non-diagnostic continuityctl entrypoints.

Solver-visible models expose EventIdentity consistency, ArchiveRecord source metadata, Replay/Lease semantics, ReconciliationSummary fields and HealthReport fields, allowing verifier assertions to be distinguished from private implementation choices.

Store interfaces show publish-attempt outcome vocabulary, the distinct poison_events durable quarantine record, processing effects/checkpoints, active replay plan filtering, lease release fencing, and retention candidate selection.

Broken starter behavior confirms the F2P suite reaches real defects including retry message-id minting, pre-ack PUBLISHED mutation, auto-approved generation changes, count/hub-sequence reconciliation, unsafe effect/checkpoint ordering, incomplete fencing and archive-only retention.

The inherited operational engine exposes production paths for replay execution, retention, health inspection and report generation; notably replay mutates item state after publish and verify/report semantics are separate from merely pre-materializing output files.
continuityctl provides diagnostic inspect/reconcile/verify and non-diagnostic generation, replay, execution, lease and retention entrypoints, including execute-replay wiring to NatsPublisher.

Seeded state makes archive, slow-consumer and active-replay retention bounds independently discriminating: east has archive gaps below its maximum, required consumers lag, and west has an approved replay plan beginning at origin sequence 5311.

findings.criterion: Verifier convergence semantics must match the solver-visible confirmed-watermark contract.
findings.why_it_matters: The contract says CONVERGED requires archive completeness through the confirmed watermark and every enabled required consumer checkpoint through that same watermark. test_f2p_reconcile_ignores_hub_sequence_equivalence explicitly sets the confirmed generation's last_observed_sequence to 60002, adds accepted+archived events at origin sequences 60000-60002, leaves every required consumer at 6000, asserts highest_contiguous_archive_origin_sequence == 6000, consumer_lag_count == 0 and converged == True. The independent final-report oracle repeats the same target=min(journal contiguous floor, archive contiguous floor) interpretation. A solver following the stated same-watermark requirement can therefore be rejected for reporting the deliberately unprocessed high-origin events as lag/divergence.
findings.minimal_remediation: Choose and state one authoritative convergence watermark semantics, then make both reconciliation tests and the independent report oracle enforce it consistently while continuing to ignore hub aggregate delivery sequence as origin identity. If the confirmed generation high watermark is authoritative, the sparse high-origin fixture must not be declared converged with consumer progress at 6000; if a contiguous accepted-origin watermark is intended instead, define that explicitly in the solver-visible contract.
findings.regression_risk: High: changing only the test expectation or only the prose can reintroduce hub-sequence coupling, hide real consumer lag, or create a new spec/verifier contradiction.

findings.criterion: Verifier assertions must grade observable publish durability rather than undocumented internal outcome vocabulary.
findings.why_it_matters: The physical-stream acknowledgement test correctly requires a wrong-stream acknowledgement to fail and leave the journal retryable, but it additionally requires the latest private publish_attempts row to have outcome exactly 'ERROR'. The delegated contract specifies journal states and the positive expected-stream acknowledgement boundary, not this publish-attempt outcome token. The token is a current store convention, not a solver-visible behavioral requirement, so this is a phantom implementation constraint.
findings.minimal_remediation: Grade the wrong-stream case by the documented observable state and acknowledgement boundary; remove the exact private outcome-token assertion unless that vocabulary is deliberately promoted into the solver-visible contract for a real operator/API reason.
findings.regression_risk: Low to medium: retain assertions that the event never becomes PUBLISHED, remains retry-eligible with the stable event id, and the acknowledgement stream is the expected physical stream.

findings.criterion: Every material reconciliation mismatch required by the delegated contract must have behavioral coverage at a model-valid reconciliation boundary.
findings.why_it_matters: The contract requires reconciliation to validate origin metadata for every matching stable identity and to produce payload checksum mismatches. The only induced metadata-mismatch F2P mutates source_domain, which validly exercises source ownership, but no test induces a model-valid payload_sha256 mismatch (or another independently mutable origin-metadata mismatch) and verifies reconciliation detects it. The final-report oracle compares payload hashes only in the already-submitted durable state; without an induced mismatch it cannot prove the reconciliation implementation detects one. A solver can omit checksum-mismatch handling and still satisfy the current suite.
findings.minimal_remediation: Add an outcome-based reconciliation case using durable state that remains deserializable/model-valid, alter an independently mutable required field such as a valid 64-hex payload checksum, and require a blocking mismatch result without failing during fixture construction.
findings.regression_risk: Medium: fixture design must preserve EventIdentity model validity so the test reaches reconciliation rather than testing deserialization failure.

findings.criterion: Poison/quarantine verification must prove durable quarantine evidence exists separately from completed business effects and progress.
findings.why_it_matters: The contract explicitly says poison input is recorded in the quarantine table. test_f2p_poison_event_is_quarantined_without_completion proves a QUARANTINED processing_effect row, zero confirmed dispatches and unchanged effect/ack checkpoints, but never asserts the separate poison_events quarantine record. An implementation that stops writing durable poison/quarantine evidence while retaining a QUARANTINED processing-effect marker can pass, leaving the operator audit requirement ungraded.
findings.minimal_remediation: In the poison path, assert the durable quarantine/poison evidence record exists for the same consumer/event while preserving the existing no-business-effect, no-dispatch and no-progress assertions.
findings.regression_risk: Low: do not reinterpret quarantine evidence as a committed business effect or advance application progress merely to satisfy the new assertion.

findings.criterion: P2P preservation tests must traverse the production boundary whose already-correct behavior they claim to protect.
findings.why_it_matters: test_p2p_distinct_same_payload_events_remain_distinct only constructs two EventEnvelope objects and compares their hashes/ids/message ids; it never sends them through publication, archive indexing, or effect deduplication. It therefore cannot prevent a production regression that incorrectly deduplicates distinct same-payload events. Likewise, the CLI preservation test completes the west archive before invoking execute-replay, so every seeded replay item can take the ALREADY_ARCHIVED/no-publish path; the NatsPublisher replay wiring can be broken while that P2P remains green.
findings.minimal_remediation: Make the distinct-same-payload preservation case pass two distinct stable identities through at least one real durable deduplication boundary, and make the execute-replay CLI preservation path exercise a non-no-op replay publication/mutation path while keeping deterministic isolation.
findings.regression_risk: Medium: preserve the legitimate no-op behavior for already archived events in a separate assertion instead of removing it.

findings.criterion: Replay fencing semantics must be unambiguous and verified across the mutation boundary where a fence can change during an in-flight publish.
findings.why_it_matters: The contract requires current owner+epoch validation before execution and again while applying replay items. The mid-plan F2P rotates the lease epoch inside the publisher after the first publish acknowledgement is produced, but then requires that first replay item be durably written as PUBLISHED under the now-stale execution token and only fences the second item. This does not distinguish per-item-entry fencing from fencing before post-publish durable recovery mutations, and it positively fixes one race interpretation that the contract does not state. A stricter solver that revalidates after the external publish returns can reasonably behave differently.
findings.minimal_remediation: Clarify the required race semantics after an acknowledgement returns under a token that became stale in-flight, then assert the chosen observable durable outcome at that exact boundary. Preserve entry fencing and between-item fencing either way.
findings.regression_risk: High: careless changes can either allow stale workers to mutate recovery state or cause duplicate replay after an already-completed external publish; the contract and test must specify the intended authority transition together.

findings.criterion: Final report correctness must be tied to the solver-visible verify entrypoint and independently cover all material health dimensions.
findings.why_it_matters: The contract says continuityctl verify writes health.json and reconciliation.json. The F2P report test independently validates files already present under /app/continuity/out but never invokes verify to produce them; the diagnostic P2P invokes verify only to check protected-state non-mutation and does not validate the generated reports. A solver can therefore pre-materialize correct static JSON while leaving verify/report-generation semantics wrong. The independent health oracle also does not validate topology_ok or retention_ok even though those are material HealthReport dimensions, so those fields can misdescribe durable/configured state without failing.
findings.minimal_remediation: Generate reports through continuityctl verify in an isolated copy of durable state, then compare the emitted reports with an independent state/config oracle including topology and retention health, while retaining the non-mutation digest check.
findings.regression_risk: Medium: the independent oracle must not call the submitted health/reconciliation implementation to calculate its expected values.

findings.criterion: The instruction's captured-incident-history preservation requirement must be meaningfully graded for every explicitly identified evidence surface.
findings.why_it_matters: The instruction explicitly identifies the archived controller log under /app/continuity/log/archive and requires captured incident history to remain intact. The report test samples incident_id/captured_at/hub source data from stream-state.json and a phrase from shift-handoff.txt, but no verifier assertion checks the archived controller log at all. A solver can delete or rewrite that captured log and still pass every current assertion.
findings.minimal_remediation: Add a preservation assertion for the archived incident controller log using stable captured evidence (for example a deterministic digest or a small set of immutable incident markers) without turning the handoff into a content-dump checklist.
findings.regression_risk: Low: preserve only the captured incident artifact, not generated/runtime logs that legitimately change during verification.

change_scope: jetstream-regional-stream-continuity/environment/continuity/docs/continuity-contract.md only where the convergence/fencing authority must be clarified
do_not_change: Do not weaken stable event identity, exact-once archive/effect semantics, generation holds, fencing, retention authority, or diagnostic non-mutation to make existing assertions easier.
Do not rewrite or delete captured incident evidence under /app/continuity/ops or /app/continuity/log/archive.
Do not turn instruction.md into a test-name inventory or hidden-verifier checklist; its current natural incident handoff shape is acceptable.
Do not use historical Q4/Q6, producer/remediation claims, Oracle/NOP results, or aggregate test counts as acceptance evidence.
next_gate: Route the observed contract/verifier defects to the authorized specification/verifier owner(s), refreeze after remediation, and run a fresh independent Q4 review before aggregate acceptance.

UNTESTED_REQUIREMENTS.gap: No induced model-valid payload checksum mismatch proves reconciliation detects/report-blocks payload divergence.
No assertion proves the separate durable poison/quarantine evidence record exists.
No production-path preservation test proves two distinct event ids with identical payloads survive durable deduplication as distinct events.
No test both invokes continuityctl verify and independently validates the reports it generated; topology_ok and retention_ok are omitted from the final independent health oracle.
No test protects the archived controller log explicitly identified by instruction.md.

AMBIGUITIES.text_or_contract: CONVERGED only when archive and every required consumer are through the same confirmed watermark.
AMBIGUITIES.interpretation_a: The confirmed generation's observed/high-water sequence is the target; events/checkpoints below it imply divergence.
AMBIGUITIES.interpretation_b: Only the highest contiguous journal/archive origin floor is the convergence target, even when the confirmed generation has observed and archived higher-origin events.
AMBIGUITIES.grading_consequence: Current tests hard-code interpretation B and assert convergence at 6000 after setting last_observed_sequence to 60002, while the prose naturally supports interpretation A or at minimum does not define B.

AMBIGUITIES.text_or_contract: Replay execution validates the current owner and fence epoch before execution and again while applying replay items.
AMBIGUITIES.interpretation_a: A fence is revalidated before every durable replay mutation, including after an external publish returns.
AMBIGUITIES.interpretation_b: Validation once at item entry is sufficient; if the epoch changes during publish, post-publish item mutation may still be written and only the next item is fenced.
AMBIGUITIES.grading_consequence: The mid-plan test requires interpretation B for the first item even though the contract does not resolve the race.

DELEGATED_CONTRACT_CHECK.observation: The instruction naturally delegates detailed durability/replay semantics to the runtime docs. The continuity-contract.md material inspected under that delegated surface contains the rules needed to reconstruct the requirements under review. Discoverability is adequate; the failures are alignment/coverage defects inside the contract-verifier relationship.
